title: We refined Orbit Chain with Codex + Fable 5 and improved our Idea Chain Model
author: WolrdInDust
selftext:
I’ve had a rougher period in life recently, and I wanted to build something that people could keep growing together, even when I’m not around or I’m having a worse time. That’s partly why I’m working on Orbit Chain and our existing Idea Chain Model. Orbit Chain is a timing game where you launch from orbit to orbit, use black-hole slingshots, and escape the rising void. The Idea Chain Model lets the winner choose what the next round adds to the game. They test it first, then the chain loops back so they can beat it again and add another idea-link. I’d love this framework to have interesting future use in games where winners help evolve the gameplay itself. We’re also adding guardrails so players can’t generate hateful/extremist/abusive rounds.

I hope you like the game and the idea of ​​the idea chain, and that anyone who plays the game can develop it.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
I think you should go with a physics based approach: allow players or miss or overshoot (bounced off geometry or fall out of orbit if the entry velocity is too high)

Point-and-snap is easier to implement but the gameplay is just too dull in my opinion

replies.author: WolrdInDust
replies.body:
Yeah, that’s actually already how it works — the clip just happened to show a pretty perfect run 😄  
Players can miss, overshoot, bounce off geometry, or fall out of orbit if they enter with too much velocity.  
I agree that pure point-and-snap would be too dull, so the goal is definitely to keep it physics/skill-based rather than automatic.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: Is it though? The orbit snap is very strong in the video; the ship literally snap to a different position and immediately uses the fixed speed assigned by the orbit

replies.author: WolrdInDust
replies.body: Is just demo, in game it is difrent - i will fix this

comments.author: argefox
comments.body:
It bothers me greatly that there's no collision. If you implement a more Newtonian physics, I think it'd be better in the overall experience, or more intuitive.

Or work with what you have but reset the stage if the user flings over a body and not around it, there's no consistent mechanics there IMO. 

Maybe keeping it fun-arcade is the right choice, I'd refine the orbital mechanics with collision and such, speed up when you get a good orbital fling, or simply not enough to make the entire trip and get stuck by orbital pull without going full Kerbal.

replies.author: WolrdInDust
replies.body:
Yeah, that makes sense — I think the demo I recorded gave the wrong impression.

There is already some skill/physics involved, but the clip showed a very clean run, so it probably looked like the player just snaps through bodies without consequences. I agree that the mechanics need to communicate failure states better: missing the orbit, overshooting, bad entry velocity, collision/bounce, or getting pulled in when you don’t have enough speed.

I don’t want to go full Kerbal, but I definitely want it to feel more physics-based and consistent, while still staying arcade and fast.
